t.4.4.1: Then Hanumān, delighted on hearing those sweetly spoken words and thinking, “He has a purpose to accomplish,” went in his mind to Sugrīva.
t.4.4.2: The regaining of the kingdom by that great-souled Sugrīva is now assured, since this man has arrived with a purpose of his own, and this very undertaking has come within reach.
t.4.4.3: Then Hanumān, the bull among monkeys, supremely delighted and skilled in speech, replied to Rāma with these words.
t.4.4.4: For what purpose have you come, together with your younger brother, to this dreadful and impassable forest adorned with the groves of Pampā and teeming with many kinds of beasts of prey and wild animals?
t.4.4.5: Hearing those words of his, Lakṣmaṇa, urged on by Rāma, described the great-souled Rāma, the son of Daśaratha.
t.4.4.6: There was a king named Daśaratha, radiant and devoted to dharma. This is his eldest son, known among the people as Rāma.
t.4.4.7: This hero, the refuge of all beings, who carries his father's command through to the end, is the most virtuous among the sons of Daśaratha.
t.4.4.8: Fallen from his kingdom, he has come here with me to dwell in the forest, the greatly radiant and self-controlled one, followed by his wife Sītā, as the greatly radiant sun at the close of day is followed by its light.
t.4.4.9: I am his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa by name, and I have entered into the service of this grateful and deeply learned man, won over by his virtues.
t.4.4.10: Of him who deserves happiness and is worthy of the highest honor, whose very self is devoted to the welfare of all beings, who has been deprived of his sovereignty and has taken to dwelling in the forest,
t.4.4.11: In a lonely place his wife was carried off by a rākṣasa able to take any form he wished, and it is not known which rākṣasa it was by whom his wife was stolen.
t.4.4.12: Danu by name, a son of Śrī, who had become a Rākṣasa through a curse, declared that Sugrīva, lord of the Vānaras, was capable.
t.4.4.13: "He, of great valour, will know the one who carried off your wife." Having spoken thus, Danu, shining brightly, went happily to heaven.
t.4.4.14: All this has been told to you, who asked, exactly as it is. Indeed, both I and Rāma have come to Sugrīva for refuge.
t.4.4.15: He who once gave away riches and won unsurpassed fame, and who was formerly the lord of the world, now seeks Sugrīva as his protector.
t.4.4.16: Now that Rāma, overwhelmed by grief and afflicted with sorrow, has come seeking refuge, Sugrīva together with the troop-leaders ought to show him favour.
t.4.4.17: To Saumitri, who was speaking thus piteously and shedding tears, Hanumān, skilled in speech, replied with these words.
t.4.4.18: Such men as these, endowed with wisdom, who have conquered anger and mastered their senses, are worthy to be seen by the lord of the vānaras; by good fortune they have come into his presence.
t.4.4.19: For he has been cast out of his kingdom and has made an enemy of Vālin; robbed of his wife, terrified, dwelling in the forest, he has been grievously wronged by his brother.
t.4.4.20: That son of the Sun, Sugrīva, together with us, will give you both his help in the search for Sītā.
t.4.4.21: Having spoken thus, Hanumān addressed Rāghava gently, in a sweet voice: "Let us go to Sugrīva."
t.4.4.22: When Hanūmān had spoken thus, the righteous Lakṣmaṇa honored him in fitting manner and then said this to Rāghava.
t.4.4.23: As this monkey, the son of Māruta, joyfully tells it, he too has come with a purpose of his own to fulfil; your purpose is as good as accomplished, O Rāghava.
t.4.4.24: His face is bright and serene, and he speaks clearly and with joy; the heroic Hanumān, son of Māruta, will not speak an untruth.
t.4.4.25: Then the greatly wise Hanumān, son of Māruta, taking with him those two heroes, the Rāghavas, went to the king of the monkeys.
t.4.4.26: Then that foremost of monkeys, the son of the Wind, of vast renown and mighty valour, delighted as one whose task is accomplished, set out for the best of mountains, he of auspicious mind, together with Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa.
